questions.prompt: The history holds two tool results in a row. How does toWire send them?
options: As two messages with role tool
As one user message holding two tool_result blocks
As one assistant message holding two tool_use blocks
As two user messages, one per result
questions.explanation: The wire has no tool role, so each result becomes a tool_result block in a user message. Neighbours with the same role are merged, so both results join one user message.

questions.prompt: A tool call in mini-dsh holds arguments as the string '{"path":"notes.txt"}'. What does the wire's tool_use block hold?
options: The same string in a field named arguments
The parsed object { path: 'notes.txt' } in a field named input
Nothing, because DeepSeek keeps its own copy of tool calls
questions.explanation: The wire format expects input as a JSON object, so toWire parses the raw arguments string into an object for the tool_use block.

questions.prompt: Why does translate yield usage and finish only when message_stop arrives?
options: So usage always comes before finish and nothing comes after finish
Because DeepSeek sends no usage before message_stop
Because message_delta never carries a stop reason
So the assembler can skip block-end pieces
questions.explanation: Output tokens and the stop reason arrive in message_delta, but waiting for message_stop keeps the shared rule: usage first, then finish, then nothing.
